target_customer: Engineering, marketing and legal teams at companies that must manage web consent and privacy compliance
problem: Consent banners and privacy controls drift from the code that ships, and compliance tools slow sites down. Inth ships an open-source consent framework with hosted monitoring and AI-assisted investigation.
business_model: Open-core: open-source c15t framework plus a paid hosted control plane (consent management, monitoring)
product_category: Consent management and privacy compliance infrastructure

founders.name: Christopher Burns
founders.background_notes: YC page: creator of c15t; speaker at Next.js Conf, Jamstack Conf and AI Engineer World's Fair; based in London. Education not listed.

technical_complexity.rationale: A framework-agnostic consent engine with regional policy packs, SDKs, server runtime and monitoring is solid engineering; SOC 2 Type 2 adds process burden.

defensibility.rationale: Open-source code can be forked and many vendors exist. Developer mindshare and embedded SDKs create modest switching costs.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copy found in sources.

market_need_then: Privacy regulations and enforcement cases keep producing consent requirements; the YC page cites c15t with over 2 million npm downloads, which is evidence of developer demand.

branding.name_origin: Company blog says the previous name Consent.io outgrew the cookie-only product and Inth was chosen for being short and memorable and signalling careful handling of user data.
branding.domain_note: Moved from consent.io to inth.com in April 2026; per search results the host was rebranded as part of the c15t 2.0 launch.

identity.voice_and_tone: Direct, plain and reassuring; candid that answers are not legal advice

branding.brand_signature: c15t, a numeronym for consent, as the open-source brand

rebrands.why: The old name fit only cookie consent; company blog gives short and memorable as the reason

branding.community_and_virality: c15t reached about 1,988 GitHub stars in one directory snapshot and over 2 million npm downloads per YC; Product Hunt launch of c15t 2.0 and conference talks.

brand_strength.rationale: The c15t open-source brand has real developer traction and talks, but the new Inth name is weeks old and the numeronym is awkward to say.

pivots.to: Compliance automation infrastructure for humans and agents (Inth)
pivots.why: Company blog says the business outgrew the consent-only name and scope

outcome_analysis: Inth grew from the open-source c15t consent library, which reports millions of downloads and conference visibility, into a broader privacy monitoring company in April 2026. It is a three person Spring 2026 team with SOC 2 Type 2 done and Vercel backing noted by YC. Outcome is open; adoption by developers is the clear strength, monetization and competition from large vendors the risk.
notes: Round is recorded as 'other' because the YC page only says backed by Y Combinator and Vercel, with no stage, amount or date. VCBacked lists pre-seed with Y Combinator, unverified. The c15t license is Apache-2.0 per the YC page and GPLv3 per SourceForge and GitHub snippets; conflicting. Everfund (Burns's earlier company) appears in aggregators with about $2.1M raised; not confirmed as the same business, so not used. Competitor list dates are not given by the directory source.
